name: CEGT Tontitown Project
researcher_notes: Not an existing row. The only Enable Gas Transmission rows are the whole system (P0161) and the MASS Expansion Project (P2560, compression only). A 2007 Federal Register notice from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission describes about 16.0 miles of new 24-inch pipe (called OM-1-A) next to existing pipe in Logan and Franklin Counties, Arkansas. It also describes a 10,310 horsepower compressor station in Le Flore County, Oklahoma. The EIA pipeline projects workbook of August 2026, historical sheet row 580, lists it as a completed new pipeline, 16 miles, 24 inches, 132 MMcf/d of added capacity, 52.3 million dollars cost, FERC docket CP08-69, in service January 2009, states OK and AR. Length is 16 mi, about 25.7 km, just over the 25 km floor, so it qualifies only narrowly. The two sources are both tied to the same project and the notice does not state capacity, cost or in-service date, so those rest on EIA alone; tier medium. Operator in 2009 was CenterPoint Energy Gas Transmission, now Enable Gas Transmission LLC under Energy Transfer; the successor is not sourced here, so Owner is the 2009 name for a person to update. A second search found no FERC order or in-service filing; the 2008 notice of application did not load with the project name. Start and end are known only at state and county level; the project name suggests Tontitown, Arkansas but the notice places the pipe in Logan and Franklin Counties, so no endpoint names were filled. No route found; official GIS was not checked.
